passages.note: House Third Reading tally shows Hoffman voting Yea on HB2492.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Chapter 99 as signed requires registration applications be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship, with rejection for noncompliance.
Bill status page lists Hoffman as prime sponsor of HB2492, signed by the Governor.

rows.reasoning: Hoffman prime-sponsored HB2492 (2022) and voted Yea on its House Third Reading; as signed into law, the bill requires registration applications be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship and directs rejection of applications lacking it, matching the rung text requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote. The 2022 House vote counts in-term under the same-legislature rule, since Hoffman served in the House before his current Senate term.
